h1: The 6 Best Pressure Cookers Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Pressure Cookers Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six pressure cookers under $100, from 6-quart multi-cookers to a stovetop pot, compared on size, functions and pot material.
summary: The Cosori 6-quart is our top pick because it packs nine functions, a ceramic-coated pot and twelve listed safety features into the sub-$100 range. The Instant Pot Duo Plus is the choice if you want a stainless steel pot and extra presets. The Instant Pot RIO Mini suits small households, and the Hawkins is the one for cooks who prefer a stovetop pot with no electronics.
intro: Most people shopping under $100 assume capacity is the only thing that separates one pressure cooker from another. It is not. The inner pot material decides whether the pot wears, and whether you are buying an electric multi-cooker or a stovetop pot decides how you will actually cook with it.

We reviewed six pressure cookers priced under $100 and ranked them on size, functions, inner pot and the type of cooker they are. We kept electric and stovetop models in one list because both meet the title, and noted which suits whom. Rankings follow listing specifications, not claimed kitchen trials.

products.name: Cosori Pressure Cooker 6QT, 9-in-1, Ceramic Coating Pot, 12 Safety Features
products.verdict: A 6-quart, 9-in-1 electric cooker with the most listed safety features.
products.description:
The Cosori is a 6-quart electric pressure cooker that bundles nine functions and lists twelve safety features. Its inner pot has a ceramic coating.

It ranks first because it delivers full family capacity and the widest function list at the lowest price among the 6-quart choices. The Instant Pot Duo Plus below it has a stainless pot and a bigger name, but it also costs more.

Buy it for a household of three to six who wants one multi-cooker. The caveat is that a coating can wear over time, so use non-metal utensils.
products.idealFor: Families wanting one capable multi-cooker on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want a stainless steel inner pot.

products.name: Instant Pot Duo Plus 6-Qt 9-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Stainless Steel
products.verdict: A 6-quart, 9-in-1 with a stainless steel pot and extra presets.
products.description:
The Duo Plus is a 6-quart electric cooker with nine functions and a stainless steel inner pot. It adds more presets than the base Duo.

It ranks second because a stainless pot lasts longer than a coating and the presets save guesswork, but pricing near the $100 line holds it below the Cosori.

Choose it if you want the Instant Pot name and a durable pot. The caveat is that the price can sit at the edge of the budget.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a durable steel pot.
products.skipIf: You need to stay well below $100.

products.name: Instant Pot 4QT RIO Mini 7-in-1 Multi-Cooker, Pressure Cooker, Slow cook, Sauté, Steam, Rice Maker, Yogurt, & Warmer
products.verdict: A 4-quart Instant Pot that suits small families at a lower price.
products.description:
The RIO Mini is a 4-quart, 7-in-1 multi-cooker from Instant Pot in a black finish. It covers pressure cooking, slow cooking, sautéing, steaming, rice, yogurt and warming.

It ranks third because 4 quarts is the sweet spot for two to three people, bigger than the 3-quart minis and cheaper than the 6-quart models.

Pick it if you cook for a couple or a small family. The caveat is that a big batch or large cut of meat may not fit.
products.skipIf: You batch cook for a crowd.

products.name: Instant Pot Duo 7-in-1 Mini Electric Pressure Cooker, Slow Rice Cooker, Steamer, Sauté, Yogurt Maker, Warmer & Sterilizer
products.verdict: A 3-quart electric cooker with a companion app for recipes.
products.description:
The Duo Mini is a 3-quart stainless steel electric cooker that does seven jobs and pairs with a companion app of recipes.

It ranks fourth because 3 quarts is tight next to the 4-quart RIO Mini. The app and the Instant Pot ecosystem are its edge for newer cooks.

Choose it for one to three people or a small kitchen. The caveat is capacity, so confirm what you normally cook will fit.
products.skipIf: You regularly cook for four or more.

products.name: OLIXIS 10-In-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, 3 Quart Multi Cooker for Rice, Stew and Steam, Small Programmable Stainless Steel
products.verdict: The cheapest programmable electric option, with ten functions.
products.description:
The OLIXIS is a 3-quart electric cooker with ten functions, programmable controls and a ceramic inner pot, priced in the $25-50 bucket.

It ranks fifth because the brand is little known next to Instant Pot and Cosori, though it has the lowest price among electric models here.

Buy it to try pressure cooking at the least cost. The caveat is that support and long-term reliability are harder to judge.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers on a tight budget.

products.name: Hawkins 3 Litre Contura Black Pressure Cooker, Hard Anodised Inner Lid Cooker, Handi Cooker, Black (CB30)
products.verdict: A 3-liter hard-anodized stovetop cooker with no electronics.
products.description:
The Hawkins Contura is a 3-liter stovetop pressure cooker made of hard-anodized metal with an inner-lid design. It uses no electricity.

It ranks last only because it lacks the multi-function convenience of the electric models. For cooks who like a stovetop pot, it is simple and has nothing electronic to fail.

Choose it if you prefer cooking on the burner. The caveat is that you must watch the heat and pressure yourself.
products.idealFor: Traditional cooks who like a stovetop pot.

methodology.title: Capacity
methodology.description: Quart and liter sizes were compared against household sizes from one person to a family.

methodology.title: Functions
methodology.description: We counted listed modes, from seven to ten, and what they replace in the kitchen.

methodology.title: Inner pot
methodology.description: Stainless steel, ceramic and hard-anodized pots were weighed for durability and care.

methodology.title: Price under $100
methodology.description: Only models in the sub-$100 price buckets were considered.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is measured in quarts or liters and sets how much you can cook at once. 3 quarts feeds one to three people, 6 quarts feeds a family. Check the quart figure in the title and avoid a pot you cannot fill to a useful level.
Electric multi-cookers regulate pressure and time for you, while stovetop pots need monitoring but are simple. Check whether the listing says 'electric' or 'stovetop' and match it to how you cook.
Stainless steel is durable, ceramic coatings are nonstick but can wear, and hard-anodized metal is tough. Look for the material in the bullets and consider how you clean.
A 9-in-1 or 10-in-1 label covers modes such as rice, sauté and yogurt. More modes help only if you use them. Read which functions are named rather than the count alone.
Pressure cookers should have lid locks and pressure release systems. The Cosori lists twelve. Check for safety features in the listing and read the manual before first use.

faq.q: Is a 6-quart pressure cooker too big for two people?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but it uses more counter space. A 3 or 4 quart model like the RIO Mini is easier for a couple.

faq.q: What mistake do first-time buyers make?
faq.a: Overfilling. Most cookers have a maximum fill line, and ignoring it risks blockages and mess.

faq.q: Is the Duo Plus worth it over the Cosori?
faq.a: If you want stainless steel and more presets, yes. Otherwise the Cosori offers similar capacity for less.
Read the manual, do a water test, and learn the pressure release method before cooking real food.

faq.q: How do I look after a ceramic-coated pot?
faq.a: Wash gently, use non-metal utensils, and avoid abrasive scrubbers to protect the coating.

faq.q: Can I use a stovetop cooker on induction?
faq.a: Check the base. The Hawkins listing does not mention induction, so confirm compatibility before buying for an induction hob.

finalTake: The Cosori 6QT is the best pressure cooker under $100 for most kitchens because it balances capacity, function and cost. Choose the Instant Pot Duo Plus for a stainless pot, the RIO Mini for a smaller household, and the Hawkins if you want no electronics at all.
